exposure: Cardiotocography (CTG) features in the first hour of labor
Clinical risk factors (e.g., thick meconium, maternal fever)
cohort: 27,927 singleton pregnancies at ≥36 weeks' gestation, cephalic presentation, with routine intrapartum CTG at a single UK tertiary site between 2001 and 2010
finding: Infants born with severe compromise had a higher proportion of abnormal first-hour CTG features (e.g., high baseline fetal heart rate, reduced variability, decelerations) and clinical risk factors (e.g., thick meconium, small for gestational age) compared to those without severe compromise.
